chunks: And with this chain, from this chain from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Uthman ibn Isa from Ibn Muskan from the one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Surely the Almighty Allah has created locks for polytheism (or evil) and made the key to those locks wine. And more evil than wine is lying.

key_terms.الْأَقْفَال: Locks (metaphor for barriers or keys to a state)

ai.seo_question: What is the key to evil according to the Imam, and what is worse than wine?
ai.summary: In this narration from Thawab al-A'mal, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the spiritual mechanism of vice, identifying wine as the 'key' that unlocks the door to greater evils, including polytheism or betrayal of trust. However, he elevates lying (al-kadhib) above wine in severity, a view supported by Shia scholars who note that while wine corrupts the body and mind, lying corrupts the truth of one's character and covenant with God. This hierarchy underscores the practical implication that truthfulness is the foundational virtue, and its loss is more detrimental than the intoxication that leads to it.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 8. And from the previous chain from al-Hassan b. Ali from Uthman b. Isa from Ibn Muskan from the one who narrated it from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
Surely the Almighty Allah has created locks for polytheism and the key to those locks is wine. There is more evil in lying than in alcohol.”
